title: yadgar/config
description: THE KNOBS THIS CHART KNOWS, AND A REFUSAL FOR EVERY OTHER KEY. Each ConfigMap is rendered from a DEEP MERGE of the chart's own chart/config/<stem>.yaml under this installation's .Values.<stem> (ADR-0721), so every property below is settable from an adopter's own repository in one line and nothing has to be cloned or forked. A document nobody overrides is still copied verbatim, comments and all; only a document with an override is re-emitted from the merged data. Helm enforces this schema in both helm lint and helm template, which is the `helm lint and render` pre-commit hook and therefore `ci / passed`, and it is also what an Argo sync meets.
$comment: `additionalProperties: false` AT EVERY LEVEL, and it never opens. It is what makes a key with no reader a REFUSAL naming the key rather than a value merged into a document nothing reads it from — the plausible mistake is not `foo`, it is `pollSecond`, and a merge that absorbed it would leave two keys looking set with one of them read. THE TYPES ARE PART OF THE REFUSAL: a values file reaches helm through sigs.k8s.io/yaml, so `pollSeconds: "30"` would arrive as a string and reach serde_yaml as one, which fails the reader at boot instead of the render. WHAT IS DECLARED HERE IS EXACTLY WHAT ONE OF THE TWO SOURCES SUPPLIES, per leaf: either chart/config/<stem>.yaml carries a default for it, or chart/consequential.yaml declares it consequential and it carries no default anywhere (ADR-0705 rule 2) — never both, and never neither. scripts/one_source_per_knob.py refuses all three of those faults at commit time. REQUIRED-NESS IS NOT EXPRESSED HERE. chart/templates/configmap.yaml calls Helm's `required` instead, because ADR-0705 asks for a refusal naming the knob AND the file, while helm's own schema error says `archive is required` on helm 3 and `missing property 'archive'` on helm 4, names no file, and is not this repository's wording to own. See the README's Blast radius section for which knobs carry a default; all three do today, which is why chart/consequential.yaml is empty. `global` IS DECLARED AND IS NOT A KNOB. Helm injects a `global` key into every subchart's values, so a closed schema with no such property makes this chart impossible to use as a DEPENDENCY at all — measured: a parent chart holding it in charts/ fails to render with no values supplied, `at '': additional properties 'global' not allowed` on helm 4.2.3 and `(root): Additional property global is not allowed` on helm 3.18.4, and ADR-0722's parent chart pinning every module chart needs exactly that. It is typed as an object and left OPEN inside, deliberately: its contents belong to the parent and to the other subcharts, this chart reads nothing from it, and refusing an unknown key under it would refuse a key another subchart legitimately reads. Nothing under `global` reaches a rendered document — the template only ever reads `.Values.<config file stem>`.

global.description: Helm's reserved key for values a parent chart shares with every subchart. This chart reads nothing from it and merges nothing out of it; it is declared so the chart can be a dependency (ADR-0722).

shared.description: Overrides for chart/config/shared.yaml — read by every service, so a change here rolls the whole estate.

pollSeconds.description: How often a process re-hashes the files it read at boot. `0` is refused at boot rather than read as `off`, so it is refused here too: it turns the watcher into a loop that re-hashes as fast as a core allows.

splayMaxSeconds.description: The top of the range each pod draws its own wait from before it exits onto a change. `0` means exit at once, which is a supported choice and not a mistake.

audit.description: Overrides for chart/config/audit.yaml — the audit module is designed and not built, so nothing reads this yet.

retentionDays.description: How long an audit record is kept. D25 is the constraint any change has to respect: an audit log with silent holes is worse than none, because it will be trusted.
